h1: Restaurant marketing in Fort Lauderdale & Broward
answer: Button Up Media is a South Florida restaurant marketing agency that helps Fort Lauderdale and Broward restaurants get found by visitors in season and keep locals coming back year-round.
heroSub: Season brings visitors who choose on their phones. The quiet months need locals. Your marketing has to handle both.

market.h2: Fort Lauderdale runs on two speeds
paragraphsHtml: From roughly December to April, snowbirds, boaters and tourists fill Las Olas, the beach and the waterfront. Many of them do not know the city well, so they choose a restaurant the way visitors always do: a search, a look at the map, a scan of photos and reviews. In season, your Google listing does more selling than your sign.

Then season ends and the pace drops. The restaurants that stay busy are the ones that kept talking to Broward residents all year, in English and Spanish, instead of going quiet online until the next winter.

Neighborhoods matter too. A room on Las Olas, a bar in the Himmarshee district, a cafe in Flagler Village and a beachfront spot off A1A are selling to different people in different moods, and your message should change with them.

needs.h2: What a Fort Lauderdale restaurant needs most

items.title: A Google listing that wins “near me” searches
items.body: When a visitor types “waterfront restaurant near me,” your Google Business Profile decides whether you show up. The right categories, real photos, accurate hours and a steady flow of reviews come first.

items.title: Reviews a visitor will trust
items.body: People who do not know the city lean on reviews. Recent ones, with real replies from you, often decide between two patios on the same block.

items.title: Content that sells the setting
items.body: The food, but also the water, the patio and the light at sunset. Short video shows a visitor what the evening will feel like. If you are on the water, make dockage or parking details easy to find.

items.title: A plan for the quiet months
items.body: Build the foundation before season and keep going after it. Content and ads aimed at locals, in English and Spanish, keep weeknights steadier when the visitors head home.

Shimuja Ramen started in Southwest Ranches, in Broward, before opening at Julia & Henry's in Downtown Miami. Its owner says many of the customers who come to try his ramen find it through the social media we run.

plan.h2: What we would do for a Fort Lauderdale restaurant

items.title: Google Maps first
items.bodyHtml: We start with your Google Business Profile: categories, photos, hours, menu and booking links, then a steady review routine with replies in both languages. For a restaurant that lives on visitors, it is often the right first step, and it is the heart of our restaurant SEO work.

items.title: Content shot at your restaurant
items.bodyHtml: Our team shoots your dishes, drinks, patio and view, then plans and posts short video and photos all year, not just in season. Here is how our restaurant social media and content service works.

items.title: Ads that follow the season
items.bodyHtml: Google Ads catch visitors searching right now, and Meta ads keep you in front of Broward locals in the slower months. Every campaign is tracked to calls, reservations or orders, so you can see what each dollar brought in. More on our restaurant Google and Meta ads.

items.title: A website built for phones
items.bodyHtml: Menu, hours, map, booking and, for waterfront rooms, dockage details a few taps away, in English and Spanish. Our restaurant website design builds that in from the start.

shoots.body: We come to your restaurant to shoot, and we schedule around your service so the floor runs normally. Patio and waterfront content is planned around the light you want on camera, and food close-ups are usually done before doors open. The same in-house team that plans your content shoots it, and one shoot typically gives us 4 to 6 weeks of content across your platforms. Planning starts with a strategy call hosted by Juan Hernandez, our founder, so the first shoot is built around your season.

A website is a one-time $1,500 (Website Build) or $2,000 (Integrated Website Build, which adds POS menu sync, reservations and ordering). Ad management has no long-term contract. faqs.q: Do you work with restaurants in Fort Lauderdale and Broward?
faqs.a: Yes. We are a South Florida team and work with restaurants across the region. One of our longtime clients, Shimuja Ramen, started in Southwest Ranches before opening in Downtown Miami.

faqs.q: How do I keep my restaurant busy after snowbird season?
faqs.a: Do not go quiet online when the visitors leave. Shift content and ads toward Broward residents, in English and Spanish, with reasons to come in on weeknights and for happy hour.

faqs.q: Should a waterfront restaurant market differently?
faqs.a: Yes. Boaters and visitors decide on their phones, so your Google listing and website should show dockage or parking, hours and menu clearly. Your photos and video should sell the view as much as the food.

faqs.q: Do you create content in Spanish?
faqs.a: Yes. Our team is bilingual, so captions, review replies, ads and your website can run in English, Spanish or both.

faqs.q: When should I start before season?
faqs.a: Ideally by early fall, ahead of the Boat Show, so your Google listing, photos and reviews are in shape and your ads are tested before the visitors arrive.
